valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 non-GAAP diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), USD per MSI common share. Anchor: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance $17.94-$17.99 (Q4 guide $5.47-$5.52; ~168M diluted shares; non-GAAP tax 21.5-22%) per the Q3 release of 2026-11-04. FY2027 EPS is my assumption (revenue growth near 8-9% from record $16.6B backlog, modest margin expansion, buybacks offsetting D-Fend/Silvus dilution and higher interest). Multiples are my judgment, not sourced peer data. Non-GAAP EPS excludes the contingent Silvus earnout charge that cut GAAP EPS to $3.06 in Q3.

bear.driver: Government/public-safety budget slowdown and acquisition integration drag: FY2027 EPS growth only ~5% from the FY2026 guide midpoint ($17.97)

base.driver: Backlog conversion with ~10-11% EPS growth, in line with the raised FY2026 trajectory

bull.driver: Record orders convert faster, margin expansion and buybacks lift EPS growth to ~15%

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $19.90 the close of $520.21 implies 26.1x; the simple average of the three named targets ($549.67) implies 27.6x on $19.90, or EPS $21.14 at a constant 26x. No horizon-documented targets exist, so no weighted analyst target is computed.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $19.90 (3.8 pp of the close); $1 of FY2027 EPS moves it by $26.
valuation.watch_metric: Non-GAAP operating margin and backlog growth (record $16.6B, +14% in Q3), which drive FY2027 EPS vs the $19.90 base
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 earnings release (expected early Feb 2027) with FY2027 guidance

analyst_notes: Only three named analysts could be sourced, plus firm-only moves reported by MarketBeat on 2026-11-05 without verified analyst names (JPMorgan $570 from $545 Overweight, UBS $570 from $520 Buy, Truist $555 from $550 buy, Piper Sandler $533 from $531 Overweight); those are excluded from the individual calculation. After the Nov 4 earnings Barclays and Evercore raised targets to $598 and $575; Morgan Stanley's $476 dates from August and predates earnings. The Evercore date is inferred from a post-earnings listing without a dated article, and no 12-month horizon was documented for any broker, so all targets have null horizons. The $549.67 named average sits about 6% above the close; relative to the base case it implies roughly 1.6 turns of P/E or about $1.24 more FY2027 EPS.
